title: Greenfire Resources Signs Acquisition Agreement With Strathcona
summary: Strathcona Resources agreed to acquire Greenfire Resources, offering 0.25 Strathcona shares or C$11.00 in cash for each Greenfire share.
body_markdown:
Waterous Energy Fund (WEF), which holds 72% of Greenfire's shares and 57% of Strathcona's, signed a support agreement and will elect the share option. Depending on elections, Strathcona expects to issue approximately 43 million to 60 million shares, or 17% to 22% of the pro forma business, and pay up to approximately C$740 million in cash. Strathcona expects Greenfire's leadership team to keep running its assets within a new business unit, SCR Central Athabasca, with Greenfire President Colin Germaniuk as its President.


The deal needs at least two-thirds of the votes cast at each company's special meeting, minority approval under MI 61-101, and Competition Act, TSX and Alberta court approvals. The release says the meetings are expected in January 2027, with closing expected shortly after.


## Why It Matters for GFR


According to the companies, the deal brings together two long-life oil sands and heavy oil businesses. The release says the combined business would hold over 3.0 billion barrels of proved plus probable (2P) reserves, a 54-year reserves life index, and would be the 4th largest SAGD operator in Canada. Year-to-date 2026 production was 34 Mbbls/d for Greenfire and 119 Mbbls/d for Strathcona, or 153 Mbbls/d combined. Strathcona said it expects approximately C$75 million of annual run-rate synergies within the first year.
